subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: Should OpenClaw keep automatic bare-text source replies as the default for direct/source and ordinary group/channel turns, or move user-facing messaging channels toward message-tool/final-only delivery with a compatibility path?
rationale: The safest leak fix intersects a compatibility-sensitive product contract: current users may rely on automatic final replies, but the field reports show automatic delivery can expose internal assistant/tool text in real channels.

options.title: Choose guarded final-only policy
options.body: Preserve existing explicit opt-outs where needed, but define a maintainer-approved message-tool/final-only policy for user-facing channels and land focused fixes/tests against that contract.

options.title: Keep automatic by default
options.body: Treat the remaining leak classes as provider/channel-specific filters and accept ongoing compatibility with bare final-text replies as higher priority.

options.title: Opt-in only for now
options.body: Land only opt-in mitigations such as stronger final-tag or message-tool modes while leaving the broader default policy open.

recommendation.title: Choose guarded final-only policy
recommendation.body: Preserve existing explicit opt-outs where needed, but define a maintainer-approved message-tool/final-only policy for user-facing channels and land focused fixes/tests against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Current main history for the central source-reply and embedded delivery paths points to vincentkoc, making them the best available routing owner for the policy/code boundary.
